items.stem: A page lists 50 enrollments and looks up each course title separately. The courses were not loaded in advance. How many queries does the database receive?

options.text: 51: one for the enrollments and one for each row.
options.feedback: One query fetches the enrollments and one more fetches each row's title. This is the N+1 pattern: one query for the list, then N more.

options.text: 1, because the page is a single request to the server.
options.feedback: One page request can trigger many queries. Each course title that was not loaded needs its own query.

options.text: 2: one for enrollments and one for courses.
options.feedback: That would happen with a join or a single extra query for all courses. The template here asks for each title separately.

options.text: 50, one for each of the enrollment rows.
options.feedback: The 50 title queries are right, but the view also ran one query to fetch the enrollments first.

items.stem: A schedule page with 3 enrollments is fast in testing. In production it lists 200 enrollments and is slow. Which explanation fits?

options.text: Queries grow with the rows: 4 in testing and 201 in production.
options.feedback: The loop runs one query for each row, so a larger table means many more queries.

options.text: The production database is always slower than a development database.
options.feedback: A slower database could add some delay. The gap here comes from 50 times more queries.

options.text: The production server runs different code from the test server.
options.feedback: The code is the same. The data is bigger.

options.text: Pages that list more text always load more slowly in production.
options.feedback: The text is short. The cost comes from the queries.

items.stem: Which change fixes the N+1 problem on the schedule page?

options.text: Fetch each enrollment with its course in one query (a join).
options.feedback: One query returns everything the template needs, so the loop makes no extra queries.

options.text: Add more workers to the server so more pages can be built at once.
options.feedback: More workers raise the number of requests the server can handle at once. Each request still makes 51 queries.

options.text: Limit the page to 10 rows and keep the same loop and template code.
options.feedback: This reduces the number of queries but keeps the pattern. A page of 10 rows still makes 11 queries.

options.text: Move the template code into the view so the loop runs earlier.
options.feedback: The queries come from asking for the course title row by row. They stay the same wherever the code is.
